title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
summary: Treat the integers as available values and find the largest run that advances by one at each step.
statement: Treat the integers as available values and find the largest run that advances by one at each step. The input may list the values in any order. Return the length of the run as an integer, counting a duplicated value once. Return 0 for an empty input. Use linear time.

examples.explanation: The values 8 through 12 form one run.

hints: Conceptual: A run can start only where the previous integer is absent.
Directional: Use a set for membership checks and loop over distinct values.
Implementation: Start counting at x only if x − 1 is missing. Probe successive integers until the first gap.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) expected time and O(n) auxiliary space. Each distinct value can be visited in only one forward run.
